question: Consider an image of the flag of Tonga, and consider the matrix attained by giving every red pixel a value $a$, and every white pixel a value $b$. What is the maximal possible rank of this matrix?

1.text:
For a rendering let $R_{i,j}=1$ if the $(i,j)$-pixel is red and $0$ if it is
white and put $J\equiv1$.  Then with the convention $a\ne b$

\begin{equation*}
M_{ij}=aR_{ij}+b(1-R_{ij})=bJ+(a-b)R ,
\qquad {\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,R .
\end{equation*}
$J$ is rank one.  On the ordinary rendering of the flag the set of red
pixels is the whole picture with the (axis parallel) white canton
$W\subset\{1,\dots ,m\}\times\{1,\dots ,n\}$ removed.  With $r\times c$
the canton

\[
R=J-W ,\qquad W_{ij}= {\bf 1}_{\,i\le r,\;j\le c},
\]

and $W=uv^{T}$ with $u_{i}= {\bf1}_{i\le r}$, $v_{j}= {\bf1}_{j\le c}$,
so that ${\rm rk}\,W=1$.  Hence

\[
M=aJ-(a-b)W
\]

is the sum of two rank-one matrices.  In particular

\[
{\rm rk}\,M\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,W =1+1=2 ,
\]

and the two rows
\[
r_{0}=(a,\dots ,a,b,\dots ,b),\qquad 
r_{1}=(a,\dots ,a)
\]
and the two columns
\[
c_{0}=(a,\dots ,a,b,\dots ,b)^{T},\qquad 
c_{1}=(b,\dots ,b,a,\dots ,a)^{T}
\]
are linearly independent as soon as the picture contains at least one
red and one white pixel and $a\ne b$.  Up to the trivial degenerate
case $a=b$, where $M\equiv aJ$ has rank $1$, the bound is attained and
in fact

\[
M=bJ+(a-b)R
\]

has exactly two non-zero singular values.  In the usual non-degenerate
normalisation this is the $2$ independent rows/columns coming from the
constant red field and from the white canton; the constant case gives
${\rm rk}M=1$.  This is the familiar rank-two ``rectangle removed from a
constant background’’ and is best possible.  If the trivial case
$a=b$ is allowed the absolute maximum is two, i.e. one in the
degenerate constant case.

5.text:
Write $J$ for the all $1$ matrix and let $R\subset [m]\times [n]$ be the set of
white pixels.  Then with $c:=a-b$

$$
X_{ij}=b+(a-b){\mathbf 1}_{R}(i,j)=bJ+cR ,
\qquad R={\mathbf 1}_{R}(i,j) .
$$

Put $R_{0}$ for the white canton.  On an idealised raster the canton is a
rectangle

$$R_{0}(i,j)=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad 
u_{i}={\bf 1}_{\{i\le r_{0}\}},\;v_{j}={\bf 1}_{\{j\le c_{0}\}} ,
$$

so $ {\rm rk}R_{0}=1$.  On the idealised picture the red emblem in the
canton is a second rectangle $R_{1}=p_{i}q_{j}$ with
${\rm rk}R_{1}=1$, and the set of white pixels is
$R=R_{0}-R_{1}$ up to the obvious inclusion of the white border of the
shield. Hence, up to the inessential $bJ$,

$$
X=bJ+cR_{0}-cR_{1}=bJ+c\,u v^{t}-c\,p q^{t},
$$

the sum of three rank one matrices.  In particular

$$
{\rm rk\,X}\le {\rm rk\,J}+{\rm rk\,R_{0}}+{\rm rk\,R_{1}}=1+1+1=3,
$$

and ${\rm rk\,X}=1$ if $a=b$.  For $a\ne b$ and for a generic choice of
the numbers of rows and columns the three matrices $J,\,uv^{t},\,pq^{t}$
are linearly independent, so that

$$
{\rm rk\,X}=3\qquad a\ne b,
$$

is attained.  Up to the harmless scalar $bJ$ this is $ {\rm rk}R=2$, i.e.
the white part of the flag is the difference of two rectangles.  In
particular with the usual idealisation the matrix is of constant rank
three; the degenerate case $a=b$ gives the constant matrix of rank one.
This is the essentially rectangular bound.  If the shield is kept with
its true curved boundary the rank of the indicator $R_{1}$ grows with the
raster, so that on the literal pixel matrix ${\rm rk}X$ can be made
arbitrarily large, bounded only by $\min\{m,n\}$, the familiar
$3$ being the rank of the idealised rectangular model.

2.text:
The $m\times n$ matrix which is obtained from the picture is a
piecewise constant matrix.  Write $J_{m,n}$ for the $m\times n$ all $1$
matrix, $r\in {\bf R}^{m}$ for the $0\!-\!1$ vector which is $1$ on the
$h$ rows of the canton and $0$ otherwise, $c\in {\bf R}^{n}$ for the
$0\!-\!1$ vector which is $1$ on the $w$ columns of the canton and $0$
otherwise and put

$$
C=r\,c^{\!T}\qquad  C_{ij}=1\iff (i,j)\ {\rm lies\ in\ the\ canton}.
$$

In the idealised picture $C$ is the characteristic matrix of the
white canton; ${\rm rk\,}C=1$.  With $R$ the characteristic matrix of
the red set we have on the idealised picture

$$
R=J-C ,\qquad 
M_{a,b}=aR+b(J-R)=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ+(b-a)C .
\tag{1}
$$

Hence, writing $d=a-b\ne0$,

$$
M_{a,b}=aJ_{m,n}+d\,r c^{T}\in {\rm span}\{J_{m,n},\,rc^{T}\},
$$

so that ${\rm rk\,}M_{a,b}\le {\rm rk\,}J_{m,n}+{\rm rk\,}rc^{T}=2$.
For $a\ne b$ the two rank-one summands in (1) are linearly
independent, so that for a generic choice of the two numbers

$${\rm rk\,}M_{a,b}=2$$

and $M_{a,b}$ has at most two independent rows and two independent
columns : the rows $i>h$ are constant $a$, the rows $1\le i\le h$ are
$b$ on the first $w$ columns and $a$ on the remaining $n-w$ columns,
etc.  In particular ${\rm rk\,}M_{a,b}\le2$ and the bound $2$ is
attained for every $a\ne b$.

If the red shield which sits in the middle of the white canton is kept
in the picture the white set is $W=C-S$ where $S$ is the characteristic
matrix of the red shield.  On the usual rectangular idealisation
${\rm rk\,}S=1$ and

$$
M_{a,b}=aJ+(b-a)(C-S)=aJ+(b-a)C-(b-a)S,
$$

i.e. $M_{a,b}$ lies in the linear span of the three rank-one matrices
$J,C,S$.  Hence

$$
{\rm rk\,}M_{a,b}\le {\rm rk\,}J+{\rm rk\,}C+{\rm rk\,}S=3,
$$

and for generic $a\ne b$ the three summands are independent, so that the
usual picture of the Tongan flag is generically a rank three matrix.
Discarding the interior shield this is the familiar rank-two
red–white canton $M_{a,b}=aJ+(b-a)rc^{T}$.  Up to the inessential
red shield this is the $2$ independent rows/columns quoted in the
literature. ∎

3.text:
The matrix is $bJ+(a-b)M_{R}$ with $J$ the all $1$ matrix and $M_{R}$ the
$0\!-\!1$ indicator of the red pixels.  Put
$$
R_{c}={\bf 1}_{\{i<h\}}{\bf 1}_{\{j<w\}}^{T},\qquad 
R_{i}={\bf 1}_{\{i_{0}\le i\le i_{1}\}}{\bf 1}_{\{j_{0}\le j\le j_{1}\}}^{T},
$$
the $h\times w$ canton and the $h_{i}\times w_{i}$ red square in the
canton.  The white part of the canton is $R_{c}-R_{i}$ and hence

$$
M_{R}=J-R_{c}+R_{i},
\qquad 
F=aJ-(a-b)R_{c}+(a-b)R_{i},
$$

is in the linear span of $J,R_{c},R_{i}$.  Each of $J,R_{c},R_{i}$ is
rank $1$, so

$$
{\rm rk}\,F\le {\rm rk}\,J+{\rm rk}\,R_{c}+{\rm rk}\,R_{i}\le 3,
$$

and $F=bJ+(a-b)M_{R}$ has the same rank as $M_{R}$.  Up to the
obvious repetition of rows the flag has only three different row–types

* $i\ge h$ : $[a,\dots ,a]$,
* $i<h,\;i\notin[i_{0},i_{1}]$ : $[b^{\,w},a^{\,W-w}]$,
* $i\in[i_{0},i_{1}]$ : $[b^{\,j_{0}},a^{\,w_{i}},b^{\,w-j_{0}-w_{i}},
a^{\,W-w}]$,

and the same three column–types.  Hence ${\rm rk}F\le3$.  For
$a\ne b$ and for a generic discretisation with $0<h_{i}<h$, $0<w_{i}<w$
the three matrices $J,R_{c},R_{i}$ are linearly independent, e.g. on a
$3\times3$ model

$$
M_{R}= \begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&0&1\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}
$$

which has rank $3$.  In particular for $a\ne b$ the matrix $F$ is
generically of rank $3$, and of course ${\rm rk}F=0$ for the degenerate
$a=b$.  This is the usual $2$–colour, $3$–region bound for the Tongan
flag. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The maximal possible rank is \(5\).

Let \(J\) be the indicator matrix of the whole flag, \(C\) the white canton rectangle, \(V\) the vertical red bar of the cross, \(H\) the horizontal red bar, and \(S=V\cap H\) the central square where they overlap. The red region is the whole flag minus the white canton plus the red cross, so its indicator is
\[
J-C+(V+H-S).
\]
Thus the two-color matrix can be written as a linear combination of the five rectangle indicators
\[
J,\quad C,\quad V,\quad H,\quad S.
\]
Each of these is the indicator of an axis-aligned rectangle, hence has rank \(1\). Therefore the rank is at most \(5\).

With a sufficiently fine pixel grid and the usual proportions of the Tongan flag, these five rectangular components occur at distinct row/column boundaries, so their contributions are independent: the all-red outside region, the white canton, the vertical arm, the horizontal arm, and the central intersection impose separate row/column modes. Hence the rank can actually reach \(5\). So the maximal possible rank is \(5\).

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is centred on how many essentially different row/column types the two-colour Tonga picture has.

* With the convention $M_{ij}=aR_{ij}+b(1-R_{ij})=bJ+(a-b)R$ the matrix lives in the span of the all-ones matrix $J$ and the red indicator $R$.  
* Idealised canton only.  On the ordinary rendering the red set is the whole $m\times n$ picture with the axis-parallel white canton $W$ removed,
$R=J-W$, $W=uv^{T}$, ${\rm rk}W=1$, ${\rm rk}J=1$.  Hence
$M=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ-(a-b)W$ is the sum of two rank-one matrices, ${\rm rk}M\le2$, and for $a\ne b$ the bound is attained.  That is the rank-two ‘rectangle removed from a constant background’ quoted by Colleague 1 and by Colleague 2 in the canton-only idealisation.  Up to the degenerate $a=b$ case this is ${\rm rk}=2$, $1$ in the constant case.

* Shield in the canton.  The real flag has a red emblem/shield inside the white canton.  Writing $C=rc^{T}$ for the canton rectangle and $S=pq^{T}$ for the (idealised) red shield rectangle, the white set is $W=C-S$ and
$R=J-C+S$.  Hence
$M=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)S$
lies in ${\rm span}\{J,C,S\}$ with each summand rank one.  So ${\rm rk}M\le1+1+1=3$.  For generic $a\ne b$ and $0<h_{i}<h$, $0<w_{i}<w$ the three matrices $J,C,S$ are linearly independent and the usual three row-types / three column-types are present, so the idealised rectangular model is generically rank three, $ {\rm rk}=1$ for $a=b$.  This is the position of Colleagues 2,3 and 5.  Discarding the inessential shield this reduces to the rank-two canton-only model.

* Colleague 4’s $5$ comes from modelling a red cross $V+H-S$ in the flag.  The Tongan flag has no cross, it has a white canton with a red shield; the $V,H,S$ decomposition is a misidentification.

* Literal raster.  Colleague 5 notes the essential point: the shield is not a true axis-aligned rectangle, it has a curved / non-rectangular boundary.  On a literal pixel image the indicator $S$ is no longer rank one; its rank grows with the refinement of the grid.  Hence on the exact pixel matrix ${\rm rk}M$ can be made arbitrarily large with resolution, bounded only by $\min\{m,n\}$.  The familiar $3$, and in the shield-free idealisation $2$, is the rank of the rectangular idealisation.

Unresolved is whether the question wants the idealised rectangular bound, $2$ with the shield ignored and $3$ with a rectangular shield, or the literal statement that the rank is unbounded in the limit of refining the image.  My current working understanding is the idealised generic bound ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically $3$, i.e. $2$ for the red-field-minus-canton model, with the caveat that the true curved shield makes the literal rank unbounded, $\le\min(m,n)$, and can be made arbitrarily large.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The matrix is $M_{ij}=b+(a-b){\bf 1}_{\rm red}(i,j)=bJ+(a-b)R$ with $J$ the all-1 matrix. Up to the harmless $bJ$ the rank is the rank of the characteristic matrix of the red set.

With the usual idealisation the red set is the whole $m\times n$ rectangle minus the white canton $W$.  $W$ is the axis-parallel rectangle $u v^{T}$ with $u_{i}={\bf1}_{i\le r},v_{j}={\bf1}_{j\le c}$ so ${\rm rk}W=1$ and $R=J-W$.  Hence $M=bJ+(a-b)J-(a-b)W$ lies in ${\rm span}\{J,W\}$ and ${\rm rk}M\le2$.  Generically for $a\ne b$ the two summands are independent and ${\rm rk}M=2$.  This is the rank-two “rectangle removed from a constant background’’ quoted by Colleagues 1 and 2.

Keeping the red emblem that sits in the canton changes the white set to
$W_{\rm white}=W-S$ where $S$ is the characteristic matrix of the red
emblem.  On the rectangular idealisation $S=pq^{T}$ is again rank one.
Then

$$M=aJ+(b-a)W+(b-a)S=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}+(b-a)pq^{T}\in{\rm span}\{J,uv^{T},pq^{T}\},$$

so ${\rm rk}M\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}uv^{T}+{\rm rk}pq^{T}=3$.  The three
matrices are linearly independent for a generic discretisation with
$0<h_{i}<h,\;0<w_{i}<w$ and $a\ne b$, so the generic idealised Tongan
flag is rank three.  Up to the $bJ$ term this is ${\rm rk}R=2$, i.e. the
white part is the difference of two rectangles.  The three row types
are $i\ge h$ constant $a$, $i<h$ outside the emblem $[b^{w},a^{n-w}]$
and $i$ inside the emblem $[b^{j_{0}},a^{w_{i}},b^{w-j_{0}-w_{i}},a^{n-w}]$
and the same three column types, so the bound $3$ is sharp.  The
degenerate case $a=b$ gives the constant matrix of rank $1$ and the
shield-free idealisation gives the familiar rank $2$.

Colleague 4’s five-term decomposition $J,C,V,H,S$ is the decomposition
that would be appropriate for a flag with a red cross in the canton.
The Tongan canton contains a shield, not a cross, so $V,H,S$ are not
present.  The $5$ bound is therefore a mis-identification of the flag.

If the true curved shield boundary is kept, $S$ is no longer rank one.
Its characteristic matrix grows with the raster and ${\rm rk}S$ can be
made arbitrarily large with the resolution, so on the literal pixel
matrix ${\rm rk}M$ can be made arbitrarily large, bounded only by
$\min(m,n)$.  The familiar $3$ is the rank of the rectangular
idealisation.  That is the usual $2$-colour, $3$-region bound for the

Write $J_{m,n}$ for the $m\times n$ all $1$ matrix and put $R_{ij}=1$ if the
$(i,j)$ pixel is red and $0$ if it is white.  With $d=a-b$

$$
M_{a,b}=aR+b(J-R)=bJ+dR ,\qquad {\rm rk}M_{a,b}={\rm rk}R
$$

up to the harmless scalar $bJ$.  Let $C$ be the characteristic matrix of
the white canton and $S$ the characteristic matrix of the red emblem
which sits in the canton.  On the usual rectangular idealisation

$$
C_{ij}=u_{i}v_{j},\qquad  u_{i}= {\bf1}_{i\le h},\;
v_{j}= {\bf1}_{j\le w},
$$

and in the same idealisation

$$
S_{ij}=p_{i}q_{j},\qquad  p_{i}= {\bf1}_{i_{0}\le i\le i_{1}},\;
q_{j}= {\bf1}_{j_{0}\le j\le j_{1}},
$$

so that ${\rm rk}C={\rm rk}S=1$.  The white set is $W=C-S$ and
$R=J-W$, i.e.

$$
R=J-C+S,\qquad 
M_{a,b}=bJ+dR=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)S .
$$

Hence

$$
M_{a,b}\in{\rm span}\{J_{m,n},C,S\},
$$

the sum of three rank one matrices.  In particular

$$
{\rm rk}M_{a,b}\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}S=1+1+1=3,
$$

and ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$ where $M\equiv bJ$.
For $a\ne b$ and $0<h_{i}<h$, $0<w_{i}<w$ the three matrices
$J,C,S$ are linearly independent.  Up to repetition of rows the flag
has in fact only the three row types

* $i>h$: $a^{\,n}$,
* $h\ge i\not\in[i_{0},i_{1}]$: $b^{\,w}a^{\,n-w}$,
* $i\in[i_{0},i_{1}]$: $b^{\,j_{0}}a^{\,w_{i}}b^{\,w-j_{0}-w_{i}}a^{\,n-w}$,

and the same three column types, so the bound $3$ is attained.  On a
$3\times3$ model e.g.

$$
R=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&0&1\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
M_{a,b}=bJ+dR,
$$

has rank $3$ for generic $a\ne b$.

$C$ alone and $R=J-C$.  Then

$$
M_{a,b}=aJ+(b-a)C=aJ+(b-a)uv^{T}
$$

is the sum of two rank one matrices, $ {\rm rk}M_{a,b}\le2$, with

3.text:
Write $J= {\bf 1}{\bf 1}^{T}$ and put $d=a-b$.  On an $m\times n$ raster let
$$
u_{c}\in\{0,1\}^{m},\qquad v_{c}\in\{0,1\}^{n}
$$
be the row and column indicators of the white canton and put
$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T}$.  Up to translation the canton is
$u_{c}(i)={\bf 1}_{i\le r}$, $v_{c}(j)={\bf 1}_{j\le c}$ so that
${\rm rk}\,C=1$ and ${\rm rk}\,J=1$.

Put $v_{v}$ for the column indicator of the vertical arm of the red
cross and $u_{h}$ for the row indicator of the horizontal arm.  With the
usual normalisation the two arms lie in the canton,
$u_{v}=u_{c}$ and $v_{h}=v_{c}$, and
\begin{equation*}
V=u_{c}v_{v}^{T},\qquad H=u_{h}v_{c}^{T},\qquad
S=V\cap H=u_{h}v_{v}^{T},
\end{equation*}
all of rank one.  The red set is the whole field with the white part of
the canton removed,
$$
R=J-C+V+H-S .
$$
Hence, with $d=a-b$,
\begin{equation*}
M_{a,b}=bJ+dR
      =aJ+d\bigl[-C+V+H-S\bigr] .
\end{equation*}
Now
\begin{equation*}
-C+V+H-S=-u_{c}v_{c}^{T}+u_{c}v_{v}^{T}+u_{h}v_{c}^{T}-u_{h}v_{v}^{T}
       =(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{v}-v_{c})^{T},
\end{equation*}
i.e. $-C+V+H-S$ is itself rank one.  In particular
\begin{equation*}
M_{a,b}=aJ+d\,(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{v}-v_{c})^{T}
\end{equation*}
lies in ${\rm span}\{J,(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{v}-v_{c})^{T}\}$.  The row
space is spanned by ${\bf 1}$ and $u_{c}-u_{h}$ and the column space by
${\bf 1}$ and $v_{v}-v_{c}$; hence
$$
{\rm rk}\,M_{a,b}\le 2,
$$
and for $a\ne b$, $r>0$, $c>0$, $0<r_{h}<r$ and $0<c_{v}<c$ the two
rank-one summands $J$ and $(u_{c}-u_{h})(v_{v}-v_{c})^{T}$ are linearly
independent.  Up to the inessential $bJ$ this is the familiar
red-field-plus-white-canton picture
$$
M_{a,b}=aJ+(b-a)C,
$$
which is the usual $2$–region, rank-two model.  In the degenerate
$a=b$ case $M_{a,b}\equiv aJ$ has rank $1$.

If the red emblem in the canton is kept as an independent axis-parallel
rectangle $S=pq^{T}$ the white set is $W=C-S$ and
$M_{a,b}=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)S\in{\rm span}\{J,C,S\}$, so that
${\rm rk}\,M_{a,b}\le3$, with ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}=3$ for generic
$a\ne b$ and $0<p_{i}<u_{c}$, $0<q_{j}<v_{c}$.  This is the three
region, rank-three idealisation normally quoted for the Tongan flag;
discarding the inessential $aJ$ it is the familiar ${\rm rk}R=2$ white
canton minus rectangular emblem picture.  The $5$–term
$J,C,V,H,S$ decomposition collapses on account of $V\subset C$,
$H\subset C$, to the two term expression above.

Remark.  On a literal pixel raster the red shield in the centre of the
canton is not a rectangle.  Its $0\!-\!1$ indicator has rank which grows
with the resolution, so for a faithful bitmap the rank of $M_{a,b}$ can
be made arbitrarily large, bounded only by $\min\{m,n\}$, the
idealised $2$, resp. $3$, being the rank of the axis-parallel model.
∎

$$

which sits in the canton.  On the usual rectangular idealisation

$$

v_{j}= {\bf1}_{j\le w},
$$

and in the same idealisation

$$

q_{j}= {\bf1}_{j_{0}\le j\le j_{1}},
$$

so that ${\rm rk}C={\rm rk}S=1$.  The white set is $W=C-S$ and

$$

$$

$$

$$

* $i>h$: $a^{\,n}$,
* $h\ge i\not\in[i_{0},i_{1}]$: $b^{\,w}a^{\,n-w}$,
* $i\in[i_{0},i_{1}]$: $b^{\,j_{0}}a^{\,w_{i}}b^{\,w-j_{0}-w_{i}}a^{\,n-w}$,

$$

has rank $3$ for generic $a\ne b$.

$$

5.text:
The matrix is $M_{a,b}=bJ+(a-b)R$ with $R_{ij}=1$ on red and $0$ on
white. Up to the harmless rank one term $bJ$ the rank is that of the
$0-1$ red indicator.

On the usual rectangular idealisation the red set is the whole
$m\times n$ rectangle with the white canton $C$ removed and the red
emblem $S$ put back.  In the idealisation

$$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},\qquad S=pq^{T}$$

with $u_{c},v_{c},p,q\in\{0,1\}^{m,n}$ the row and column indicators of
the canton and of the red shield.  Hence ${\rm rk}C={\rm rk}S=1$ and

$$R=J-C+S,\qquad 
M_{a,b}=bJ+(a-b)R=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)S\in{\rm span}\{J,C,S\}.$$

In particular

$${\rm rk}M_{a,b}\le {\rm rk}J+{\rm rk}C+{\rm rk}S=3,$$

and ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$ where $M\equiv bJ$.

* $i$ outside the canton: $a^{n}$,
* $i$ in the canton but outside the emblem: $b^{w}a^{\,n-w}$,
* $i$ in the emblem: $b^{j_{0}}a^{w_{i}}b^{\,w-j_{0}-w_{i}}a^{\,n-w}$,

and the same three column types.  For $a\ne b$ and $0<h_{i}<h$,
$0<w_{i}<w$ the three rank-one summands $J,C,S$ are generically
linearly independent.  For instance on a $3\times3$ model

$$R=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&0&1\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
M_{a,b}=bJ+(a-b)R,$$

has ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}=3$ for generic $a\ne b$.  Discarding the inessential
constant $bJ$ this is the familiar ${\rm rk}R=2$ ``red field minus a
white rectangle’’ model

$$M_{a,b}^{0}=aJ+(b-a)C,\qquad {\rm rk}M_{a,b}^{0}\le2,$$

with ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}^{0}=2$ for $a\ne b$ and $1$ for $a=b$.  The

cross, so the independent modes are $J,C,S$.

arbitrarily large with resolution.  The $3$, and up to the harmless

Write $J$ for the $m\times n$ all $1$ matrix and $d=a-b$. Up to the harmless

\end{equation*}

for the $0\!-\!1$ indicator of the red emblem which lies in the canton.

\begin{equation*}
C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},\qquad S=pq^{T},
\end{equation*}
${\rm rk}C={\rm rk}S=1$, and with $W=C-S$ the white set

\begin{equation*}
R=J-W=J-C+S .
\end{equation*}
Hence, up to the constant,

\begin{equation*}
M_{a,b}=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)S\in {\rm span}\{J,C,S\},
\end{equation*}
and

\begin{equation*}
{\rm rk}M_{a,b}\le 1+1+1=3,
\end{equation*}
with ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}=1$ for the degenerate $a=b$.  Up to repetition the
flag has the three row types

* $i$ outside the canton : $a^{n}$,
* $i$ in the canton but outside the emblem : $b^{\,w}a^{\,n-w}$,
* $i$ in the emblem : $b^{\,j_{0}}a^{\,w_{i}}b^{\,w-j_{0}-w_{i}}a^{\,n-w}$,

are linearly independent and the bound is attained, e.g. on a

M_{a,b}=bJ+dR,
\end{equation*}
has rank $3$ for generic $a\ne b$.  In particular ${\rm rk}R=2$ and

white canton and red emblem, idealisation.  Discarding the interior
emblem $S\equiv0$ we get the familiar red field minus a white rectangle
model

\begin{equation*}
M_{a,b}^{0}=aJ+(b-a)C=aJ+(b-a)u_{c}v_{c}^{T}\in{\rm span}\{J,C\},
\end{equation*}
${\rm rk}M_{a,b}^{0}\le2$, ${\rm rk}M_{a,b}^{0}=2$ for $a\ne b$ and
${\rm rk}M_{a,b}^{0}=1$ for $a=b$, the usual rank two ``constant

\begin{equation*}

\end{equation*}

flag, $2$ for the canton only and $3$ for the canton with a rectangular

I agree with the rank-3 consensus. Writing \(M=bJ+(a-b)R\), the only independent features are the constant red field, the white canton, and the red emblem inside the canton. The cross can of course be described geometrically as a vertical bar plus a horizontal bar, but that is not a rank decomposition: the two bars overlap inside the same emblem, and their union is still just the emblem indicator. Once the white canton is separated out, there is no genuinely new fourth row/column direction. The apparent distinction between rows through the vertical arm and rows through the horizontal arm is a subdivision within the same emblem, not an independent mode.

So the rank is at most \(3\), and for \(a\ne b\) on a nondegenerate raster the three terms \(J\), the canton indicator, and the emblem indicator are independent. Rank \(2\) ignores the emblem; rank \(4\) would double-count the two arms of the cross as separate features. The sharp answer is \(3\).

Keeping the red emblem in the canton as an idealised axis-parallel rectangle $S=pq^{T}$, ${\rm rk}S=1$, the white set is $W=C-S$ and $R=J-C+S$.  Then $M=aJ+(b-a)C+(a-b)S\in{\rm span}\{J,C,S\}$ so ${\rm rk}M\le3$, generically ${\rm rk}M=3$ for $a\ne b$ with $0<h_i<h$, $0<w_i<w$, and ${\rm rk}M=1$ for $a=b$. $$M_{a,b}=bJ+dR,\qquad R_{ij}=1_{{\rm red}}(i,j),$$

$$C=u_{c}v_{c}^{T},\qquad u_{c,i}={\bf1}_{i\le h},\;v_{c,j}={\bf1}_{j\le w},$$
